extraction.name: LongVid
extraction.description: LongVid is a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types (video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting), supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios. Videos are curated from Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, encompassing movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos of long duration. The dataset contains 300,000 hours of videos and 2 billion words of textual annotations.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
extraction.publisher: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology (Chinese Academy of Sciences), Shanghai Innovation Institute
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongVid leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. Dense event labels are generated for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions (Panda-70M for HD-VILA, CosMo for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D, and original high-quality captions from MiraData). Consecutive segments are filtered and regrouped into long video sequences, then a sequence of event labels with corresponding timestamps is constructed for every long video based on their captions. For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), these are directly utilized as event labels, while for others, major events are extracted from captions using an LLM. Finally, several types of long video QA pairs are constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps of short video segments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Videos sourced from four open-source video datasets: Ego4D (3,662 long egocentric videos), HowTo100M (more than 1 million long-duration how-to videos), HD-VILA (large-scale in-the-wild videos), and MiraData (large-scale minute-level movie segments). Captions sourced from Panda-70M (for HD-VILA), CosMo/HowToInterlink7M (for HowTo100M), Ego4D-HCap (for Ego4D), and original MiraData captions.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Ego4D: hierarchical captions from Ego4DHcap are used; short video captions are concatenated to form dense captions for longer segments. For MiraData: an open-source LLM (Qwen-72b) is used to extract event and background labels from main object and background captions. For HowTo100M: HowToInterlink7M provides refined interleaved video captions; HTStep provides temporal annotations of instructional steps. For HD-VILA: consecutive video segments are filtered that can be reconstructed into more than 60s long videos from the 10M training subset; event labels are extracted from captions using an LLM in the same way as MiraData.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Consecutive short video segments are filtered and regrouped into long video sequences (minimum 60 seconds for HD-VILA). For datasets without high-quality event-level annotations, major events are extracted from captions using an LLM. QA pairs are constructed across five task types: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. For stage 2 pre-training, most captions are refined using AI models to ensure richer and more detailed descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are derived from existing dataset annotations and LLM-generated labels. For Ego4D: Ego4DHcap hierarchical captions are used directly; event relation recognition tasks use short video captions as event labels; temporal grounding uses short video captions with corresponding timestamps. For MiraData: Qwen-72b LLM extracts event and background labels from captions; event/background relation recognition ground truth is formed by ordering labels of a long video. For HowTo100M: HTStep large-scale dataset provides temporal annotations of instructional steps. For HD-VILA: Panda-70M captions are used; event labels are extracted from captions using an LLM. The Multi-Hop Needle in a Video Haystack benchmark uses human-annotated captions and QA pairs from MS-COCO.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen-72b LLM (for extracting event and background labels from captions), VideoChat2 (for recaptioning video description data), Gemini (for recaptioning detailed video description data), LLava-NeXT-34B (for recaptioning detailed image description data), GPT-4o (for annotating short video instruction data)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables MLLMs to process and understand long-form videos including movies, documentaries, surveillance videos, and online video streams. The model trained on this data demonstrates the ability to detect anomalous behaviors in surveillance videos (e.g., catalytic converter theft), which has potential applications in public safety and security monitoring.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The existing long video training corpus lacks the instruction-following paradigm (video, instruction, answer triplets) crucial for multimodal reasoning. The dataset is constructed from specific source datasets (Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, MiraData) which may not cover all video domains equally.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for long video understanding tasks including: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. The dataset supports a multi-stage short-to-long learning scheme for video MLLMs.
